cosy-lesson.title: The Maze of Biases : Surviving Our Cognitive Flaws

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Loss aversion – the psychological phenomenon where the pain of losing is twice as powerful as the pleasure of gaining.

p.em: Example: Due to intense loss aversion, she chose to keep her secure, boring job rather than starting a business.

cosy-blockquote.p: Status quo bias – the cognitive preference for the current state of affairs, viewing any change as a loss.

p.em: Example: The company's resistance to remote work was a textbook case of status quo bias.

cosy-blockquote.p: Halo effect – the cognitive bias where our overall impression of a person influences how we feel about their character.

p.em: Example: The attractive candidate benefited from the halo effect, as the board assumed he was highly competent.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dunning-Kruger effect – the cognitive bias where people with limited competence overestimate their own abilities.

p.em: Example: His arrogant confidence during the negotiation was a classic display of the Dunning-Kruger effect.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sunk cost fallacy – the behavior loop of continuing an endeavor because of previously invested resources.

p.em: Example: Clinging to a failing project simply because you spent years on it is the sunk cost fallacy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cognitive humility – the awareness of the limitations and fallibility of one's own mind and knowledge.

p.em: Example: Practicing cognitive humility prevents us from falling into the trap of ideological dogmatism.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heuristic – a mental shortcut that allows people to solve problems and make judgments quickly.

p.em: Example: While a heuristic saves time, it often introduces systematic errors into our financial decisions.

cosy-blockquote.p: Audit – a systematic, critical inspection of one's own beliefs, finances, or decisions.

p.em: Example: Conducting a regular cognitive audit helps us identify which biases are currently dictating our choices.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distortion – the alteration of original data, creating a false or misleading cognitive representation.

p.em: Example: Her memory of the conflict was a complete emotional distortion designed to protect her ego.

cosy-blockquote.p: Overconfidence – the subjective state of holding unwarranted confidence in one's own judgment or skills.

p.em: Example: His overconfidence during the stock market boom led to a devastating financial loss.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does Loss aversion prevent us from making necessary, courageous career changes?
★ Have you ever held onto a bad investment or relationship due to intense Loss aversion ?

Why is Status quo bias the primary enemy of innovation in traditional corporate environments?
★ How do you personally fight off Status quo bias when planning your annual goals?

How does the Halo effect distort our capacity to evaluate the real competence of public figures?
★ Have you ever realized you liked a colleague simply because they had an attractive appearance?

Why does the Dunning-Kruger effect seem to thrive so intensely on modern social media platforms?
★ Have you ever suffered from the opposite of Dunning-Kruger-imposter syndrome-in your career?

How does the Sunk cost fallacy trap us in unfulfilling relationships and obsolete professions?
★ When was the last time you walked away from a project, successfully defeating the Sunk cost fallacy ?

Why is cultivating Cognitive humility the ultimate defense against ideological manipulation?
★ In what specific area of your life do you need to practice more Cognitive humility right now?

How do evolutionary Heuristic shortcuts cause systematic errors in modern financial planning?
★ What is your favorite cognitive shortcut when forced to evaluate a stranger's character quickly?

What are the practical benefits of conducting a weekly cognitive Audit of our emotional triggers?
★ How do you audit your own thoughts when you feel a sudden surge of irrational anger?

In what ways does emotional stress introduce severe cognitive Distortion into our memories?
★ Have you ever discovered that your memory of a major family event was a complete Distortion ?

Why is professional Overconfidence often rewarded in corporate leadership while humility is ignored?
★ Has your own Overconfidence ever led you to make a significant professional mistake?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: The Bias Audit: Imagine you are auditing a corporate board that is completely blinded by overconfidence and sunk cost fallacies. Present your critique using at least one second conditional, one third conditional, and one mixed conditional.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li: If you stopped letting Loss aversion dictate your investments tomorrow, would you take more calculated risks?
If society completely abandoned its Status quo bias , do you think we would achieve total progress faster?
If your brain were immune to the Halo effect , would you evaluate people with absolute objectivity?
If you had recognized the Dunning-Kruger effect in your previous boss, would you have resigned much sooner?
If they had walked away from that failing project years ago, would they have saved millions today?
If we had cultivated more Cognitive humility back then, would we have avoided that ideological conflict?
If that mental Heuristic had not saved your ancestor's life, would you be sitting here discussing psychology today?
If you had conducted a rigorous cognitive Audit last year, would you now feel more aligned with your values today?
If your memory had not introduced that protective Distortion , would your self-concept be shattered today?
If your Overconfidence had been checked by a wise mentor, would you have avoided that major business mistake?

ul.li: Incorrect: I suggest to read the article → Correct: I suggest reading the article ((Suggest + -ing))
Incorrect: The brain trick us → Correct: The brain tricks us ((Depends on))

Incorrect: I was sympathizing with her struggles → Correct: I was empathizing with her struggles / showed deep empathy ((Linguistic register: 'sympathize' suggests feeling pity, while 'empathize' implies a deeper psychological understanding and shared feelings))

Incorrect: We discussed about the psychological impact → Correct: We discussed the psychological impact / had a discussion about the psychological impact ((Underlined prepositional error. Better collocation: 'discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'))
Incorrect: I have 25 years old → Correct: I am 25 years old ((Age with 'to be'))
